posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
I do like how challenge Dreamer forces you to re-prioritize your plays and discards. Get Out of the Way, for instance, becomes instant discard fodder, you'll never want to play it.

That said, the fight for me came down to just the Scholar (no surprise), and then I forgot that being at low health means I should really have Flesh to Iron out, so he didn't last forever like he probably could have. :( A decent set of support incaps, at least.

posts.name: starkenburg_alexander
posts.cooked:
Mint, but yeeowch. 0/0/12/0

I think that is the longest game of the Dreamer I have ever actually won. I thought things were going to go bad (well, even worse than they already were) when Idealist dropped on the third round due to Monster of Id I couldn't find any other Concepts to feed to it. Surprisingly, Setback, Luminary, and Scholar all proceeded to live (barely) for quite a long time, slowly plinking away at manifestations. Lots of random card discarding from environment or Setback meant that I never actually saw a Night Terrors that would have ended things faster. Luminary hid behind her bots, Scholar Ironed, Setback just did Setback things to stay alive, and Idealist fed Scholar cards to keep his forms in play.

Eventually, Dreamer had to shuffle her deck while still on her front side(!!!), but eventually we got all the manifestations. She flipped, and things were going alright again but Mordengrade was getting out of control. I was getting worried until Luminary drew the Terraluna Translocator with ~30 cards in her trash and 5 Manifestations in play. Bip Bop Boop, dropping the moon on the manifestations took us to 7 of 8 under Dreamer (I was VERY careful to not target the ones already under her) and cleared Mordengrade. From there, both Setback and Luminary went down to some combination of plays I don't remember, but Scholar was fine behind Iron and had enough damage to destroy Mr. Bones for the win.

Weird notes: No AoE as has been pointed out, due to challenge. ALSO, no Backlash Generators for the same reason. Setback barely survived the flip due to putting out extra ongoings to keep Silver Lining in play. The Toymaster is actually useless in this match as no one uses Equipment. The Tanks actually helped during the Plan: Drop the Moon on Them!(TM) as they played an additional manifestation that I could destroy.

Was overall fun because I minted, but whoo boy I don't know that I want to try again on the PC

~Komori

Nope. Can't figure this one out. First try, got nuked off the field as soon as the Dreamer flipped by a double Violent Nightmares into Night Terrors. Second try, Scholar had 2x FTI out and was doing a great job until he got hit with Projected Paralysis FOUR TURNS IN A ROW while the Dreamer slowly got her entire board out, then wiped me with Night Terrors. posts.name: QuirkyDM
posts.cooked:
Near Mint, due to my careless use of Backlash generators in game 1 once Dreamer flipped.

Besides the backlash generators, both games turned out about the same. I put Scholar behind an iron wall (2xFlesh to Iron) early on and he soaked up most of the damage, as did the repair drones who are immune to melee damage. Idealist played Bored Now! on turn 1 to get rid of Monster of Id until her ego was in better shape. Damage was prioritized to Macabre Spirit, Dark Hero, Grotesque Arachnoid, Tooth Fairy and Treacherous Ape. The rest, I ignored since they couldn't cause any damage, but picked them off if I had extra damage to spare. Scholar spent the game drawing cards and healing when he could. Except for the annoying Blade Battalion Platoon, the environment was never a problem and was usually quite helpful.

Eventually, with everyone decently set up, the last manifestation went down and Scholar plunked down Alchemical Redirection for the next two turns. It took three turns to get enough manifestations under Dreamer, but everyone still was at 10 or higher, with Luminary at about 18 and Scholar at full.
